artifacts.description: Quartus Prime Pro EDA netlist export (Version 26.1.0 Build 110 03/26/2026 SC Pro Edition)

missing: no carry-chain adder of at least 4 bits
no fixed rotation in the wiring between banks

method.description: Walks the netlist graph produced by hal_agilex.vo_netlist: register chains, carry chains, pure-wire bit maps and LUT cones. No solver and no simulation.
method.name: structural crypto pattern match

findings.summary: ARX needs adders, rotations and an XOR layer together; no carry-chain adder of at least 4 bits; no fixed rotation in the wiring between banks
findings.title: No ARX round structure

evidence: 17 bijective non-affine substitution(s) extracted from LUT cones, 17 of them matching the built-in library

method.description: Walks the netlist graph produced by hal_agilex.vo_netlist: register chains, carry chains, pure-wire bit maps and LUT cones. No solver and no simulation.
method.name: structural crypto pattern match

findings.summary: The structures found (spn) are the ones classical symmetric primitives are built from, and no lattice/ring arithmetic was found. This does NOT rule out post-quantum cryptography: a hash-based or code-based scheme contains neither NTTs nor S-boxes and would come back none-detected here.
findings.title: Classical / PQC style: classical-style

evidence: 17 bijective non-affine substitution(s) extracted from LUT cones, 17 of them matching the built-in library

method.description: Walks the netlist graph produced by hal_agilex.vo_netlist: register chains, carry chains, pure-wire bit maps and LUT cones. No solver and no simulation.
method.name: structural crypto pattern match

findings.summary: The six passes agree on 'spn'. Families with evidence: spn. Every line of the evidence list below is a structural observation; none of them names an algorithm.
findings.title: Structural family: spn

missing: no add/subtract pair over the same operand registers
no carry chain with a constant operand, so no modulus to read

method.description: Walks the netlist graph produced by hal_agilex.vo_netlist: register chains, carry chains, pure-wire bit maps and LUT cones. No solver and no simulation.
method.name: structural crypto pattern match

findings.summary: A butterfly needs an add and a subtract over the same operands, and a modulus needs a constant operand; no add/subtract pair over the same operand registers; no carry chain with a constant operand, so no modulus to read
findings.title: No modular-arithmetic transform

method.description: Walks the netlist graph produced by hal_agilex.vo_netlist: register chains, carry chains, pure-wire bit maps and LUT cones. No solver and no simulation.
method.name: structural crypto pattern match

findings.summary: Every pure-wire map between two equally wide vectors is the identity, so there is no permutation layer to compare against the published pLayers.
findings.title: No non-identity bit permutation layer

assumptions.description: Input and output bits were ordered by net name, which is the pass's own convention; a match at the 'bit_permutation' tier is exactly the statement that a different order would make the tables equal.
tennm_lcell_comb and tennm_ff behave as documented in hal_agilex.primitives, which was validated by simulating real Quartus exports against the RTL they were synthesised from.
The .vo reader refuses Verilog it does not understand, so no instance can have been dropped silently before the analysis ran.

bounds.description: the cones are combinational, so enumerating their input space covers every evaluation of them

data.bit_permutation_search: bit-permutation equivalence searched exhaustively (4! input permutations)

method.description: Enumerates the whole input space of a combinational cone using only the tennm_lcell_comb semantics in hal_agilex.primitives, and reads the truth table off it. Exhaustive, so the resulting table is the function, not a sample of it.
method.name: exhaustive cone evaluation

scope.description: LUT cones over kreg[15], kreg[16], kreg[17], kreg[18]

notes: Structure-bounded claims only: every finding is about what the netlist is wired to compute, never about what the design is for.
none-detected is a result, not a failure: it means none of the six passes fired, and the per-pass findings say what each one looked for.
